Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
In what year was Marie Curie born?
Marie Curie: Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
In what year was Nitroglycerin discovered?
Nitroglycerin: It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
In what year was Thallium discovered?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
Ceftriaxone: Pfizer. Ceftriaxone, sold under the brand name Rocephin, is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
In which country is Convair B-58 Hustler based?
Convair B-58 Hustler: United States. The Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight.
Who is credited with discovering Dubnium?
Dubnium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Dubnium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Db and atomic number 105.
Who is credited with discovering Brainfuck?
Brainfuck: Urban Müller. Brainfuck is an esoteric programming language created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller.
Who is credited with discovering Cobalt?
Cobalt: Georg Brandt. Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Home to both edible and poisonous species, this fungal genus supplies the West's most popular cultivated mushrooms, including the everyday button mushroom — which genus is it?
Agaricus is a genus of mushroom-forming fungi containing both edible and poisonous species, with over 400 members worldwide and possibly again as many disputed or newly discovered species.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and almost always monogamous breeders, which bird family unites ducks, geese, and swans under one scientific name?
Anatidae are the biological family of water birds that includes ducks, geese, and swans.
Native to Europe and Asia, which genus of burdock plants owes its seed-dispersal success to burrs that later inspired a famous fastening invention?
Arctium is a genus of biennial plants commonly known as burdock, family Asteraceae.
Created in 1989 by Brian Fox for the GNU Project as a free replacement for the Bourne shell, this command-line interpreter became the default login shell on countless Linux systems — which shell?
Bash (Unix shell) (short for "Bourne Again SHell") is an interactive command interpreter and command language developed for Unix-like operating systems.
Native to India and Nepal, this medium-sized antelope sports a striking two-tone coat, with males growing corkscrew horns up to 75 cm long. Which animal is it?
Blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.
This small leafy vegetable, a cultivar of cabbage grown for its edible buds, shares its name with a European capital — what is it?
Brussels sprout is a member of the Gemmifera cultivar group of cabbages (Brassica oleracea), grown for its edible buds.

This American astronomer and planetary scientist was initially an assistant professor at Harvard before moving to Cornell as the David Duncan Professor of Astronomy. He played an active role in the Voyager programs. Who is he?
Carl Sagan (November 9, 1934 - December 20, 1996) was an American astronomer, planetary scientist and science communicator.
Patented in 1948 and used to treat hay fever and other allergic conditions, this first-generation antihistamine works within two hours by blocking the H1 histamine receptor — name the drug?
Chlorphenamine (CP, CPM), also known as chlorpheniramine, is an antihistamine used to treat the symptoms of allergic conditions such as allergic rhinitis (hay fever).

This highly venomous, nocturnal snake, black or bluish-black with narrow white crossbands, is widely distributed across South Asia, from grasslands to agricultural fields to human settlements — what snake is it?
Common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
Its name comes from the Greek for "dark blue," and its anion — a carbon triple-bonded to nitrogen — is so toxic that salts like the sodium and potassium forms cause swift poisoning. What is it?
Cyanide (from Greek kyanos 'dark blue') is an inorganic chemical compound that contains a CN functional group.
This Russian chemist's great law let him predict three undiscovered elements — germanium, gallium, and scandium — and a synthetic element now bears his name; who was he?
This Russian economist served as Vladimir Putin's economic adviser before becoming governor of her country's central bank, and was ranked among Forbes' most powerful women in 2019 — who is she?
Elvira Nabiullina (born 29 October 1963) is a Russian economist and current governor of the Central Bank of Russia.
This sensory organ detects light and converts it into electro-chemical signals in neurons, using an adjustable lens system to focus incoming light and form images — name the organ?
Eye is a sensory organ that allows an organism to perceive visual information.
He worked on uranium enrichment during the Manhattan Project, then — after McCarthyism cost him his physics post — founded San Francisco's hands-on Exploratorium museum; who was he?

Frank Oppenheimer (August 14, 1912 - February 3, 1985) was an American particle physicist, cattle rancher, professor of physics at the University of Colorado, and the founder of the Exploratorium in San Francisco.
The largest and outermost of the three hip muscles, this one shapes the buttocks and helps keep the human trunk upright — what muscle is it?
Gluteus maximus is the main extensor muscle of the hip in humans.
Though usually grouped with the birch family, some botanists split this deciduous shrub genus into its own family — and its nut is a popular snack — which plant?
Hazel are plants of the genus Corylus of deciduous trees and large shrubs native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
Named for a Greek youth beloved by Apollo and slain by a jealous wind god who then transformed him into this fragrant spring bloom — what flower genus is it?
Hyacinth is a genus of bulbous herbs and spring-blooming perennials.
Resembling a lump of burnt charcoal growing on birch bark, this parasitic fungus is popularly called chaga — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus (a Latinization of the Russian word), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
Holder of 128 firearm patents, this American engineer invented the telescoping bolt that made compact autoloading pistols possible — who is he?

John Browning (January 23, 1855 - November 26, 1926) was an American firearm designer who developed many varieties of military and civilian firearms, cartridges, and gun mechanisms, many of which are still in use around the world.
Despite its name suggesting a root vegetable, this biennial cultivar of wild cabbage grows a swollen edible stem above ground and is related to broccoli, kale, and Brussels sprouts — what is it?
Kohlrabi (scientific name Brassica oleracea Gongylodes Group), also called German turnip or turnip cabbage, is a biennial vegetable, a low, stout cultivar of wild cabbage.

Named after the Italian word for lemon, this colorless liquid hydrocarbon is the main compound behind citrus peel fragrance, occurring mostly as a right-handed form extracted commercially by centrifugal separation or steam distillation - name the compound?

Limonene is a colorless liquid aliphatic hydrocarbon classified as a cyclic monoterpene, and is the major component in the fragrance and essential oil of citrus fruit peels, taking its name from Italian limone ("lemon").
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, quokkas, and tree-kangaroos among its 63 living species — what family is it?
Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
This nitrogen-heavy compound forms durable plastic resins used in dry-erase boards and dinnerware, and its foam version scrubs stains as the innards of a Magic Eraser — name the chemical?
Melamine is an organic compound with the formula C3H6N6.
This SI base unit for amount of substance, symbol mol, is defined so that one unit contains exactly 6.02214076×10²³ elementary entities — what is it called?
Mole (unit) (symbol mol) is a unit of measurement, the base unit in the International System of Units (SI) for amount of substance.

The first recognized fossil of this archaic human group was unearthed in 1856 in a German valley, and the species vanished around 40,000 years ago as modern humans arrived; who were these Pleistocene Europeans?

Neanderthal (nee-(r)-TAHL, nay-, -THAHL; Homo neanderthalensis or sometimes Homo sapiens neanderthalensis) are an extinct group of archaic humans who inhabited Europe and Western and Central Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene.

Synthesized in 2002 at a lab near Moscow and named in 2016 for the physicist who hunted down the heaviest atoms, this synthetic element claims the highest atomic number and atomic mass of anything yet known — which is it?
Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Found in organs such as the brain and lungs, inside flatworms, and within leaf cross-sections, this word names an organism's bulk functional tissue — what is it?
Parenchyma is the bulk of functional substance in an animal organ such as the brain or lungs, or a structure such as a tumour.
Made in the body from the amino acid L-phenylalanine, this natural stimulant also turns up in fermented chocolate and inhibits a transporter called VMAT2 — what is it?
Phenethylamine (PEA) is an organic compound, natural monoamine alkaloid, and trace amine, which acts as a central nervous system stimulant in humans.
It looks like a single point of light, but this brightest star of Ursa Minor is actually a triple star system parked near the north celestial pole — what is it?
Polaris is a yellow supergiant star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Minor.
This noncontagious autoimmune condition leaves dry, scaly patches of skin and can flare at the exact spot of an injury — a quirk called the Koebner phenomenon; what is it?
Psoriasis is a long-lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterized by patches of abnormal skin.

This condition, often triggered by crush injuries or extreme exercise, causes skeletal muscle to break down so rapidly that it can turn urine tea-colored and damage the kidneys — what condition is it?
Rhabdomyolysis (shortened as rhabdo) is a condition in which damaged skeletal muscle breaks down rapidly.
Contracted from contaminated food, this bacterial illness typically causes diarrhea, fever, and cramps within a day or two of exposure — what is it called?
Salmonellosis is a symptomatic infection caused by bacteria of the genus Salmonella.
Cartilaginous and toothy, these fish are the sister group to the rays and skates and trace their ancestors to the Devonian Period — what are they?

Shark are a group of elasmobranch cartilaginous fishes characterized by a ribless endoskeleton, dermal denticles, five to seven gill slits on each side, and pectoral fins that are not fused to the head.
This leafy green vegetable's high oxalate content gives raw and cooked versions noticeably different flavors, with blanching helping to tone it down — what vegetable is it?
Spinach (Spinacia oleracea) is a leafy green flowering plant native to Central and Western Asia.
This South African biologist established the tiny roundworm C. elegans as a model organism, work that helped earn him a share of the 2002 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Who was he?
Sydney Brenner (13 January 1927 - 5 April 2019) was a South African biologist.

Beloved by biologists for its wild morphological variation and elaborate nest-building, this northern fish tolerates big swings in salinity, living in the sea but breeding in fresh water — what is it?
Three-spined stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) is a fish native to most inland and coastal waters north of 30N.
These large, heavyset American game birds have a distinctive fleshy growth called a snood hanging from the base of their beak, with wild and ocellated species. What birds are they?
Turkey (bird) are large, heavyset galliforms in the genus Meleagris, indigenous to the Americas.
This pungent Japanese condiment, ground from the rhizome of a plant related to horseradish and mustard, traditionally accompanies sushi. What is it?

This teenage prodigy's work on solvable polynomials helped birth what's now called group theory, and his fiery Republican politics landed him in prison before a fatal duel ended his life at 20 — who was he?
Évariste Galois (25 October 1811 - 31 May 1832) was a French mathematician and political activist.
Recognizable by its black-and-white striped legs and a lyre-shaped marking on its thorax, this mosquito native to North Africa spreads dengue and yellow fever worldwide — what is it?
Aedes aegypti: Species of mosquito. The mosquito can be recognized by black and white markings on its legs and a marking in the form of a lyre on the upper surface of its thorax.
This diverse group of photosynthetic organisms ranges from microscopic plankton to seaweeds 50 metres long — yet excludes the land plants entirely. What is it?
Algae: Diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. Algae (AL-jee, UK also AL-ghee; sing.: alga) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms.
Nominated by Donald Trump in 2020, this Notre Dame law professor became the fifth woman to serve as a US Supreme Court associate justice after previously sitting on the Seventh Circuit — who is she?

Amy Coney Barrett: US Supreme Court justice since 2020. Barrett graduated from Rhodes College before attending Notre Dame Law School, earning a Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree in 1997 and ranked first in her class.
Originating from the heart's left ventricle, this is the largest artery in the human body, eventually splitting into the two common iliac arteries in the abdomen — what is it?
Aorta: Largest artery in the human body. The aorta distributes oxygenated blood to all parts of the body through the systemic circulation.

First catalogued in 1729 by an Italian priest who thought its spore-forming structures resembled a holy-water sprinkler, this genus of several hundred mold species takes its name from the Latin word for 'to sprinkle' — which genus?
Aspergillus: Genus of fungi. Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
One of the first grains ever domesticated, around 9000 BC in the Fertile Crescent, this cereal now ranks fourth in world production — and 70% of it goes to feeding animals — what is it?
Barley: Cereal grain. Barley (Hordeum vulgare), a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.
Split into structural biology, enzymology, and metabolism, this scientific field studies the chemical processes that occur within living organisms — which field?

Biochemistry: Study of chemical processes of living organisms. Biochemistry, or biological chemistry (distinct from chemical biology), is the study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.

Bred in South Africa as a family guard dog, this large mastiff-type breed has a short coat and heavy bone structure, and is recognized by that country's kennel union but not the international federation — what breed is it?
Boerboel: South African breed of dog. The Boerboel (pronounced [ˈbuːrbul]) is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
An intact, more muscular and aggressive adult male of the cattle species, this animal has long been a sacrificial symbol in many religions and stars in famous arena sports. What is it?
Bull: Adult male cattle. A bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
Indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains and grown across Asia and Africa largely for hashish production, this plant species carries far more THC than industrial hemp — which species is it?
Cannabis indica: Species of plant. Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Its edible 'curd' is actually a dense head of undeveloped flower buds, and one variety grows its curds in spiral fractal patterns — which vegetable?
Cauliflower: Vegetable in the species Brassica oleracea.
Traceable to fairy tales that weren't classified this way until the seventeenth century, this genre spans picture books for toddlers to young-adult fiction for teens — what category of writing?
Children's literature: Stories, books, magazines, and poems primarily written for children.
This spore-forming, rod-shaped bacterium produces the most potent toxin known to science, causing a severe paralytic illness often linked to bulging canned food — what's its name?
Clostridium botulinum: Species of endospore forming bacterium.

This grayish-brown, wart-skinned amphibian (scientific name Bufo bufo) is found across most of Europe, hides by day, and hunts invertebrates at dusk, moving with a slow, ungainly walk or short jumps — which species?
Common toad: Species of amphibian. It belongs to a group of closely related species descended from a common ancestral line of toads and forming a species complex.
Originating in French cuisine and beloved in Spain, this breaded, deep-fried roll often reuses leftover roasted chicken or broth meat as its filling — what is it called?

Nicknamed the 'Wooden Wonder' for its mostly-timber airframe, this WWII British warplane was among the fastest operational aircraft of 1941 and later moonlighted as a high-speed courier for a national airline — what was it?
De Havilland Mosquito: British multi-role combat aircraft of WW2.
This category of mental health conditions involves an unconscious defense mechanism that fragments consciousness, memory, and identity to protect against traumatic stress — what is it called?
Dissociative disorder: Set of mental health conditions.
Its leaves and flowers are covered in dense white hairs that shield it from Alpine cold and UV rays, making this daisy-family flower a symbol of mountaineering purity — what is it?
This outermost skin layer ranges from about 31 micrometers thick on delicate areas to nearly 600 micrometers on the sole of the foot — what is it?
Epidermis: Outermost of the three layers that make up the skin.

One of the few birds known to pass the mirror test, this highly intelligent corvid found across the northern reaches of Eurasia has a nidopallium proportionally as large as a chimpanzee's brain — which bird is it?
Eurasian magpie: Species of bird. The Eurasian magpie or common magpie (Pica pica) is a resident breeding bird throughout the northern part of the Eurasian continent.
Reproducing via spores rather than seeds or flowers, this group of vascular plants unfurls from coiled 'fiddleheads' into fronds and numbers over 10,000 species — what are they?
Fern: Class of vascular plants. The group includes about 10,560 known extant species.
With atomic number 87 and a most stable isotope whose half-life is just 22 minutes, this alkali metal is the second-rarest naturally occurring element on Earth — which one?
Francium: Chemical element with atomic number 87 (Fr)

Sold under a non-proprietary name once the original patent expires, this type of medication shares the same active ingredient as its brand-name predecessor, though packaging and coloring may differ — what's it called?
Generic drug: Pharmaceutical equivalent to a brand-name product.
First selectively bred for color in imperial China over 1,000 years ago, which popular aquarium pet has become an invasive pest after being released into rivers in North America and Australia?
Goldfish: Freshwater fish common in aquariums.
Born Herman Mudgett and dubbed the 'Beast of Chicago,' this con artist and serial killer worked his most notorious crimes around the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition — who was he?
H. H. Holmes: American con artist and serial killer (1861–1896)
This Michigan farm boy left home at 16 for Detroit, later patented the Model T's transmission, and gave his name to a whole system of mass production. Who was he?
This British Egyptologist discovered the untouched tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings in November 1922 — who is he?
Howard Carter: British archaeologist and Egyptologist (1874–1939)
This 14th-century Arab scholar wrote his most famous work, the Muqaddimah, in just six months and once met the conqueror Tamerlane — who is he?
Ibn Khaldun: Arab Islamic scholar, historian and philosopher (1332–1406)
This Russian physiologist won the 1904 Nobel Prize for his work on digestion, but is far better remembered for training dogs to salivate at a signal — who was he?
Building his first firearm at age 13 in his father's gun shop, this American designer earned 128 patents and pioneered the autoloading pistol — who is he?
Marketed as Nizoral, this antifungal medication also treats Cushing's syndrome and excess hair growth in women, though oral use risks liver damage — which drug?
This probability principle explains why a casino might lose money on a single spin of roulette but reliably earns a predictable percentage over many thousands of spins. What is it called?
Law of large numbers: Averages of repeated trials converge to the expected value.
Patented in 1978 and approved for use in the US in 1987, this ACE inhibitor is a common first-line treatment for high blood pressure — what drug is it?
Lisinopril: Medication used to treat hypertension and heart failure.
Named from a Greek root meaning 'light' or 'brightness' in reference to its luminous, reflective eyes, this genus includes the bobcat among its four wild cat species — which genus?
Lynx: Genus of medium-sized wild cats.
A Russian pediatric endocrinologist also known by the surname Faassen, this woman is the elder child of Russia's president. Who is she?
Maria Vorontsova: Daughter of Vladimir Putin (born 1985)
This mammal family — skunks and stink badgers — was reclassified out of the weasel family in the 1990s after genetic evidence, and turns out to be closest kin to red pandas and raccoons. What is it?
Mephitidae: Family of mammals. In taxonomic order, the living species of Mephitidae are:.
With over 17,000 built and flown by more than 50 countries, this Soviet-designed twin-turbine machine is the most-produced helicopter in the world — what is it?
Mil Mi-8: Family of transport helicopters.
Its wings make an odd whistling sound on take-off, and one pair may raise up to six broods a year — which abundant North American gamebird?
Mourning dove: North American bird in the family Columbidae.
Descended from Southern Italy's traditional guard dogs and closely related to the Cane Corso, this large wrinkly Italian breed was recognized in 1949 — which dog breed?
Neapolitan Mastiff: Italian breed of dog. The Neapolitan Mastiff or Mastino Napoletano is an Italian breed of large dog of mastiff type.
Introduced to Hawaii in 1929, this crested songbird serves as the state bird of seven US states including Ohio and Virginia — which bird?
Northern cardinal: Species of North American bird.
A woody perennial native to the Mediterranean and a close relative of sweet marjoram, this mint-family herb is a staple of Italian and Greek cooking — what is it?
This skin sensation includes the classic 'pins and needles' feeling when a limb falls asleep, and can also be triggered by hitting your funny bone — what is it called?
Paresthesia: Dermal sensation with no physical cause.

Caused by a lack of intrinsic factor — often from an autoimmune attack on the stomach — this vitamin B12 deficiency disorder brings gradual fatigue, a smooth red tongue, and numbness in the hands and feet — which condition?
Pernicious anemia: Lack of red blood cells due to vitamin B12 deficiency.

The most economically important member of the bromeliad family, this South American fruit became a 17th-century European symbol of luxury — and forms when many small flowers fuse into one — what is it?
Pineapple: Species of flowering plant in the family Bromeliaceae.
This deliquescent white salt helps make Dutch-process cocoa, soap, and glass, and can also turn up leaking from old alkaline batteries — what compound?
Potassium carbonate: Chemical compound. It is a white salt, which is soluble in water and forms a strongly alkaline solution.

Also known as talk therapy, this practice uses regular personal interaction to help people change behavior and improve well-being, with effects research suggests often outlast those of medication — what is it called?
Psychotherapy: Clinically applied psychology for desired behavior change.

Distinguished from its smaller cousin mainly by size rather than any strict taxonomy, this long-tailed rodent genus numbers 56 known species, with 'kangaroo' and 'bandicoot' variants named for their appearance — which rodent?
Recognizable by its long, black-and-white ringed tail, this highly social Madagascar primate lives in troops of up to 30 and is dominated by females — which species?
Ring-tailed lemur: Species of mammal from Madagascar.
Native to the North Atlantic and North Pacific, these anadromous fish hatch in freshwater gravel beds, mature in the ocean, then return to their birth river to spawn — what are they?

Caused by a sudden burst of synchronized electrical activity in the brain, this neurological event affects roughly 50 million people worldwide and can range from a brief blank stare to a full convulsion — what is it?
Seizure: Period of symptoms due to excessive or synchronous neuronal brain activity.
This layer of tissue covering a vertebrate's body serves three main functions: protection, regulation, and sensation?
Skin: Soft outer covering organ of vertebrates.

First described in 1915 by a German paleontologist from Egyptian fossils that were destroyed during World War II, this dinosaur genus wasn't represented by new material until the early 2000s — which genus?
Spinosaurus: Genus of spinosaurid dinosaur. The genus was known first from Egyptian remains discovered in 1912 and described by German palaeontologist Ernst Stromer in 1915.
The first variable-sweep-wing aircraft to enter Soviet service, this fighter-bomber was produced from 1967 to 1990 and exported in variants flown across the Arab world — which jet?
Sukhoi Su-17: Soviet variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber. The Sukhoi Su-17 (Russian: Су-17; NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
Also known as estragon, this perennial herb in the daisy family comes in a French variety prized for cooking and a milder Russian variety — which herb?
Tarragon: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae.
After dropping out of Stuyvesant High School and serving in the Korean War, this economist went on to earn a PhD from Chicago and a National Humanities Medal in 2002?
Co-founder and former CEO of a ride-hailing giant, this businessman resigned in 2017 amid allegations he ignored harassment reports, later selling most of his shares for $2.5 billion — who is he?
Travis Kalanick: American entrepreneur and former CEO of Uber.
This medical condition occurs when kidney failure allows urea and other metabolic waste products to build up dangerously in the bloodstream. What's it called?
Uremia: Excess urea in the blood due to kidney dysfunction.
Known as the 'true foxes,' animals in this genus are smaller and bushier-tailed than any wolf or jackal, with a signature dark triangular mask between the eyes — which genus?
Vulpes: Genus of true foxes. The members of this genus are colloquially referred to as true foxes, meaning they form a proper clade.
Made up of eight carpal bones and home to the carpal tunnel and the anatomical snuff box, this joint connects the hand to the forearm — which body part?
Wrist: Part of the arm between the lower arm and the hand.
